clues: This city stands along a river in the west of a long thin land in south Europe. Its old town spreads over seven hills by the water.
Summers here are hot and dry, with long bright days and little rain. Winters turn mild and wet, the flip side of those dry months.
Long ago this city ruled a vast empire as the seat of its rulers. In 1871 it became the capital of a newly united land, and it still is.
Gladiators once fought wild beasts in a huge stone ring here, the largest old arena still standing. It went up nearly 2,000 years ago and still draws crowds.
The chiefs of Italy rule the land from this city. A whole tiny land, the Pope's own, sits inside its bounds, a land in a city.
